business_scope.primary_industry_name: Open-Market Brokerage of Solid-State Drives and Server Processors

meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Common Law (English common law heritage, blended with Fa'a Samoa customary law in land and social matters; international company matters governed by dedicated statute)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: PACER Plus (Pacific Agreement on Closer Economic Relations Plus)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Money Laundering Prevention Act 2007 (Samoa), as amended; Financial Intelligence Unit Act 2007; International Companies Act 1987, as amended by the International Companies (Amendment) Acts 2017 and 2018; International Companies (Registered Agents) Regulations 2017; FIU AML/CFT Guidelines for Reporting Entities; obligations consistent with Asia/Pacific Group on Money Laundering (APG) mutual evaluation standards.
ubo_and_aml_profiling.ubo_disclosure_level: Government_Only_Access - UBO records are maintained by the SIFA-licensed registered agent in Samoa; no public registry inspection; mandatory on-demand disclosure to the Samoan Financial Intelligence Unit, the Registrar of International Companies, and other competent law-enforcement agencies; nominee arrangements permitted but the nominator's beneficial owner must be fully disclosed to the registered agent.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing of ultimate corporate shareholder (if any)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent companies registrar in the shareholder's jurisdiction of incorporation

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized Power of Attorney appointing the Samoan licensed registered agent
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public in the signatory's jurisdiction

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified passport copies and proof of address for all directors, shareholders, and ultimate beneficial owners
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public or competent issuing authority in the document's country of origin

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Draft Memorandum and Articles of Association (English-language, with optional Chinese parallel text in non-statutory annex)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Licensed Samoan registered agent or international legal counsel
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization in Samoa (domestic issuance; no apostille required)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference letter or professional reference letter for each ultimate beneficial owner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Issuing bank or regulated financial institution

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Affidavit / declaration of beneficial ownership for the Samoa International Company
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Licensed Samoan registered agent before a Samoan notary public
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization in Samoa (domestic issuance; no apostille required)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory risk-based customer due diligence and enhanced due diligence under the Money Laundering Prevention Act 2007 and FIU directives; screening must cover the Samoa domestic sanctions list, United Nations Security Council consolidated list, OFAC SDN list, and EU consolidated financial sanctions list; all domestic and foreign PEPs require senior management approval, source-of-funds verification, and enhanced ongoing monitoring; given the Medium_Risk_Enhanced AML tier for open-market semiconductor brokerage, all Swift_TT and escrow-inspection wire transactions are subject to enhanced transaction monitoring, threshold reporting, and suspicious-transaction reporting to the Samoa FIU.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Samoa International Finance Authority (SIFA) - International Companies Registry online name search and reservation portal (sifa.ws)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The registered legal name must be rendered in Latin/English script; Samoan words are permissible if verified by the Registrar; a Chinese parallel name may be adopted in the articles of association as an informational annex but carries no statutory effect at the registry; misleading transliterations of prohibited or sensitive tokens are rejected.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon rejection, the applicant (acting through the licensed registered agent) may file a written reconsideration request with the Registrar of International Companies within 14 working days; if reconsideration is refused, a de novo application with a new name may be submitted with payment of the applicable fee; further administrative appeal lies to the Samoa International Finance Authority; ultimate judicial review is available before the Supreme Court of Samoa under the Judicature Ordinance 1961; a rejected name reservation is not automatically extended and requires a fresh filing.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permissible for operational purposes - the statutory registered office must be the physical office of the SIFA-licensed registered agent in Samoa; no separately leased premises, local staff, or physical commercial establishment is required for an offshore International Company engaged in spot semiconductor trading and brokerage.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low - approximately 5-10% probability of an unannounced inspection during the first three years for a fully compliant medium-risk International Company; SIFA and the Financial Intelligence Unit retain statutory on-site inspection rights over registered agents and entity records, with trigger probability rising upon sanctions-list hits, third-party payment anomalies, or irregular Swift_TT / escrow wire flows.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: International Companies Act 1987 (Samoa), as amended (ss. 4-9 on incorporation, ss. 13-16 on share capital); administered with the Samoa International Finance Authority Act 2003
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Samoa International Finance Authority (SIFA) - International Companies Registry, Apia, Samoa
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Application for Incorporation (Form IC-1) with executed Memorandum and Articles of Association, filed through a SIFA-licensed Registered Agent
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital for an International Company; initial issued capital may be nominal (e.g. 100 ordinary shares at USD 1.00 each); no escrow or deposit account required by law
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED that 100 ordinary shares of US$1.00 each be allotted and issued to the founding subscriber, constituting the Company's entire initial issued share capital. RESOLVED that the registered office in Samoa be fixed at the office of the licensed Registered Agent, Apia, and that the said Agent be authorized to receive service of process. RESOLVED that the following officers be and are hereby appointed: [Name] and [Name] as Directors, and [Name] as Secretary, each serving until the next general meeting. RESOLVED that the Directors execute all filings necessary with the Samoa International Finance Authority and open an escrow wire-receivable bank account.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: SIFA Registry - International Companies Unit, Apia (submission through a licensed registered agent or SIFA online portal)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit Form NC-01 with up to three proposed names in English, each ending with 'Limited' or 'Ltd.'. SIFA searches the Register and issues a Name Reservation Certificate valid for 30 days. Restricted words (e.g. Bank, Trust, Insurance) and names confusingly similar to existing entities are rejected.
required_dossiers: Passport copy of applicant incorporator or licensed agent covering letter
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: File an objection with SIFA or immediately resubmit on an amended proposed name; apply for a 30-day extension of the reservation before expiry.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Preparation of Memorandum and Articles of Association
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: SIFA-licensed Registered Agent (corporate services firm in Samoa)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the Memorandum and Articles of Association in English; include the name, registered office clause, registered agent clause, object clause authorizing international wholesale brokerage of electronic components (SSD and CPU), and capital clause. The incorporator executes both documents; the registered agent countersigns consent.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Circulate a written requisition to counsel; execute redlined amendments and re-sign only the affected pages before filing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Filing of Incorporation Application with SIFA
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: SIFA Registry - Registrar of International Companies
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File Form IC-1 in triplicate accompanied by the executed Memorandum and Articles, statutory declarations of each director, registered agent consent, notice of registered office, and payment of the USD 100 government fee. SIFA verifies name availability, director qualifications, and agent licensing before approving.
required_dossiers: Executed Memorandum and Articles of Association
Statutory declaration of solvency and good repute for each director
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Respond to SIFA requisition via a Cure Notice within 14 days; amend the defective schedule and re-file without a new application fee if the requisition is procedural.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: SIFA Registry - Registrar of International Companies
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon approval, the Registrar issues the Certificate of Incorporation bearing the company number and date of incorporation, at which time the Company acquires legal personality. Immediately thereafter, file the Notice of Directors and Secretary and order share certificates and the company seal.
required_dossiers: Form IC-2 Notice of Directors and Secretary (post-completion filing)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Request a certified true copy or duplicate certificate by filing Form D-01 with SIFA and paying the prescribed search/certification fee.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-Incorporation Governance and Bank Account Opening
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Board of Directors, SIFA-licensed Registered Agent, and a licensed commercial bank in Samoa
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Convene the first board meeting or adopt written shareholder resolutions approving the First Board Resolution, allotting shares, appointing officers, and opening a corporate bank account capable of receiving SWIFT TT and escrow inspection wire payments. Ensure full KYC and beneficial ownership files are compiled for the bank's Enhanced Due Diligence review.
required_dossiers: Register of Directors and Register of Members
Corporate KYC pack (passports, proof of address, corporate chart)
Beneficial ownership declaration for AML/CFT compliance
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Re-run EDD/KYC checks if the bank queries beneficial ownership; provide a Samoan legal opinion confirming the Company's valid existence and the directors' authority.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Samoa International Finance Authority (SIFA) for corporate authorization; Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour (MCIL) for any ancillary domestic trade matters - none applicable to offshore wholesale brokerage
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: No industrial operating permit required; the Certificate of Incorporation issued under the International Companies Act 1987 constitutes the sole statutory authorization for cross-border wholesale brokerage of SSD and CPU components

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Planning and Urban Management Agency (PUMA) under the Ministry of Natural Resources and Environment (MNRE)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt - Category A; administrative office use within existing commercial premises; no land disturbance or significant discharge, therefore no EIA report or registration required
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No wastewater or VOC thresholds are triggered by office-based trading. If physical inventory is warehoused on-site, comply with non-hazardous goods storage protocols under the Waste Management Regulations; defective or end-of-life components must be consigned to an MNRE-licensed e-waste recycler.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire Safety Certificate issued by the Samoa Fire and Emergency Services Authority (SFESA) upon biennial inspection of the registered office; compliance with the Samoan Building Code for office occupancy load limits; occupational safety clearance under the Labour and Employment Relations Act 2013 including emergency signage, first-aid provision, and evacuation plan approval.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Ministry for Revenue (MfR) of the Government of Samoa, Apia — the national revenue authority administering income tax, VAGST, and customs; taxpayer-facing portal and e-filing services are delivered through the MfR e-Tax system, while International Company incorporation and the statutory register are maintained by the Registrar of International Companies under the Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Foreign applicants: (1) incorporate the Samoa International Company under the International Companies Act 1987 through the Registrar of International Companies; (2) obtain Certificate of Incorporation, constitutional documents, and registered agent appointment; (3) apply for a 9-digit TIN at the Ministry for Revenue on Form TR-1, attaching certified incorporation documents, constitutional documents, director and beneficial-owner registers, and the Samoan registered-agent certificate; (4) no further tax registration is required because the IC is statutorily exempt from Samoan income tax and VAGST on international income; (5) pay the annual International Company government fee to the Registry to preserve tax-exempt status.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Tax_Exempt_Zone: the Samoa International Company is a non-resident, tax-exempt vehicle; international wholesale brokerage income from SSD and server CPU chip trading is excluded from Samoan entity-level taxation, and the IC has no Samoan territorial tax nexus beyond its registered office and agent.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No US-style check-the-box election exists under Samoan law. Available mechanisms: (i) application to MfR for a Certificate of Residence or Non-Resident Tax Certificate evidencing exempt status; (ii) a constitutional-election to convert or redomicile the IC into a domestic taxable company, thereby accepting entity-level domestic taxation (generally inadvisable); (iii) US beneficial owners may file Form 8832 to treat the IC as a disregarded entity or partnership on US returns, which has no Samoan tax effect; (iv) Samoa, as an OECD Inclusive Framework member, applies general anti-avoidance recharacterization under the Tax Administration Act 2015 to hybrid mismatch arrangements, with no elective hybrid mismatch rule currently legislated.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Goods and Services Tax (VAGST) under the Value Added Goods and Services Tax Act 2003, administered by the Ministry for Revenue.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: Compulsory VAGST registration arises when taxable supplies made in Samoa exceed WST 100,000 within any 12-month period. An International Company conducting purely offshore wholesale of semiconductor goods normally has no Samoan taxable supplies and therefore falls outside this threshold.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No real-time fiscal clearance, digital stamping, or continuous transaction control (electronic-invoicing/API) mandate is currently in force in Samoa. VAGST returns are filed electronically via the MfR e-Tax portal and customs declarations are processed through the ASYCUDA World platform, with no statutory API invoice-clearance obligation as of the current regime.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: A VAGST-registered supplier may zero-rate: (a) goods physically exported from Samoa within 28 days of the time of supply to a recipient outside Samoa, provided contemporaneous proof of export is preserved; and (b) services supplied to a non-resident who is outside Samoa at the time of supply, where such services are not performed in Samoa and are not directly connected with Samoan land or goods located in Samoa. The International Company may claim zero-rating only where the chips or services actually transit or are supplied from Samoa; principal-to-principal trading executed wholly offshore outside Samoa does not enter the Samoan VAGST base and requires no zero-rating claim.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (ASYCUDA SAD) as cleared by Samoa Customs
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill evidencing export consignment to the foreign buyer
Inward Remittance Certificate or SWIFT/MT103 confirmation evidencing foreign currency repatriation
VAGST export declaration / zero-rating worksheet maintained under the VAGST Act 2003
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Unsupported or fraudulent export zero-rating claims trigger: (i) reassessment and retrospective clawback of refunded VAGST with statutory interest under the Tax Administration Act 2015; (ii) civil shortfall penalties of up to 150% of the avoided tax for evasion; (iii) criminal fines of up to WST 50,000 and imprisonment for responsible directors or officers; (iv) extended audit windows of up to 10 years (unlimited in fraud cases); and (v) potential revocation of the International Company's tax-exempt status with reclassification to full domestic taxation of historical profits.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Central Bank of Samoa (CBS), established under the Central Bank of Samoa Act 2005, exercising foreign exchange authority under the Exchange Control Act 1975 and the Exchange Control Regulations 1976, operating through licensed authorized dealers (commercial banks).
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Samoa has accepted IMF Article VIII obligations; the Samoan Tala (WST) is administratively convertible for bona fide current-account transactions through licensed authorized dealers, but the WST is not freely traded internationally and has no genuine offshore interbank market. Capital account transfers, resident foreign-currency accounts, and any WST conversion by a resident require CBS application-based approval. The WS_IC is a non-resident, tax-exempt International Company (IC); all SSD/CPU trade proceeds are collected and paid in USD outside Samoa. Profit remittance to non-resident shareholders is executed USD-to-USD without entering the WST market and therefore does not trigger CBS exchange-control approval. The only practical remittance hurdle is documentary: the bank will require proof of the IC's good standing, tax-exemption status, and a representation that no Samoan resident holds ownership or benefits from the remitted profits.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Statutorily, under the Exchange Control Regulations 1976, a resident exporter must repatriate full export proceeds within 90 days of shipment and surrender 100% of the foreign currency to an authorized dealer unless an approved foreign-currency account or a CBS exemption certificate is held. The target operation is structured as an offshore open-market relay: the IC purchases SSD components and server CPUs from, and sells them to, non-resident counterparties, with title passing outside Samoa and no goods entering Samoan customs territory. In that configuration, no Samoan export declaration arises and the 90-day surrender rule is not engaged. If any future physical export from Samoa occurs, the mandatory 100% surrender timeline will apply unless a CBS-approved USD account exemption is pre-arranged.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Offshore USD Operational Current Account with segregated Capital Escrow sub-account
USD Operational Current Account plus Capital Escrow Account for inspection wires
Foreign-Currency Operational Account (USD and major currencies)
Local retail-focused account; not designed for International Company non-resident structures

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low - structurally non-viable as a settlement spine. Samoa has no electronic-money-institution (EMI) licensing or passporting regime; the Money Remitters Act 2016 licenses only domestic CBS-supervised remittance businesses. Offshore digital EMIs (e.g., Wise- or Payoneer-type platforms) are neither recognized nor accepted as source-of-funds evidence by Samoan banks, and the IC's wholesale purchase and sale obligations must clear over SWIFT through a CBS-licensed authorized dealer to preserve an audit-grade trail. An EMI may be used only as an ancillary commission-collection layer, never as the primary clearing rail.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical attendance by overseas directors is generally waivable. Account opening proceeds through a licensed Registered Agent under the International Companies Act 2012; the bank requires a certified certificate of incorporation, board resolutions appointing signatories, notarized and apostilled passport copies of all natural-person ultimate beneficial owners, banker's references from home-country relationships, and source-of-wealth statements. A video or in-person KYC interview is mandatory when any beneficial owner is a PEP, when a discretionary trust or nominee appears in the ownership chain, or when counterparty geography includes higher-risk Asian clearance hubs. ANZ and BSP are the most accommodating for fully remote onboarding; Bank of Samoa and National Bank of Samoa may still impose a physical visit to Apia.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Concealed or nominee-heavy ownership chain (bearer share arrangements or discretionary trust without disclosed beneficiaries) inconsistent with the IC's tax-exempt status.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Full cascading beneficial-ownership chart to natural persons; trust deed and protector letter; beneficial-ownership register extract lodged with the Registered Agent; sworn source-of-wealth declarations; the Registered Agent's licensed client due-diligence file; and audited financial statements or an accountant's letter evidencing an operational rather than shell profile.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-velocity, thin-margin spot trades in SSDs and server CPUs with multi-hop counterparties in Hong Kong, Singapore, and China, including third-party logistics chains.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Per-tranche transaction file: purchase order, proforma invoice, commercial invoice, SWIFT MT103 payment evidence, airway bill or bill of lading, and proof of delivery/receipt; a treasury flow process map matching purchase and sale legs; per-tranche margin explanation; counterparty KYC and negative-news screening reports; and the IC's written AML/business-conduct policy aligned with Financial Action Task Force standards.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Suspicious payment patterns: remitter name or settling bank differs from the contractual counterparty, rapid in-and-out movements, or use of aggregation accounts.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Remittance-matching ledger keyed by invoice number; Registered Agent certification of counterparty banking details; correspondent bank credit advices retained for at least seven years; executed director-level attestation against third-party intermediation; and a standing instruction that no payee may be added unless KYC-cleared and transaction-linked.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Export-control and sanctions exposure in the semiconductor hardware chain (SSD controllers, server CPUs) flowing through China or Hong Kong toward unknown end-users.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Technical classification memo citing ECCN and HTS codes; per-buyer end-user and end-use certificates; UN/EU/OFAC/CBS sanctions screening outputs including beneficial-ownership screening of all buyer entities; documented no-resale-to-sanctioned-party undertaking; annual compliance review prepared via an approved screening platform; and CBS or Registered Agent notification whenever a flagged jurisdiction becomes a payment destination.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Non-resident shareholders remit paid-in capital by SWIFT MT103 in USD to the IC's dedicated Capital Escrow Account at the Samoan authorized dealer. The remittance must be labeled as direct investment - paid-in capital of an International Company, and the account package must include the board capital-call resolution, shareholder register, Registered Agent good-standing letter, and a non-resident representation confirming that no Samoan resident holds an interest. Because no WST conversion and no resident payment is involved, CBS exchange-control approval is not triggered; the bank nevertheless records the debit in its CBS-reportable balance-of-payments capital ledger. Any shareholder subordinated loan must be notified to the CBS if aggregate external debt exceeds the Samoan reporting threshold or if funds are subsequently converted into WST.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Supplier payments are executed by SWIFT MT103 priority transfers from the IC's USD account, cleared through ANZ Bank's Australia relationships or BSP's Pacific-region correspondent network. For delivery-assured wholesale purchases, an irrevocable sight documentary letter of credit is opened with ANZ or BSP Samoa and may be confirmed by a top-tier Singapore or Hong Kong bank, with payment made against compliant presentation of transport and warranty documents. Outbound trade disbursements are purpose-coded as general merchandise imports (or trade-related services for commissions) and supported by commercial invoice plus airway bill or bill of lading. Disbursements above CBS monitoring thresholds require an exchange-control application form (CBS EC-type filing) prior to dispatch; the bank will impose a 24-hour hold on unusually large or mismatched drafts pending CBS clarification. For escrow-protected deals, buyer funds are cleared into the bank's segregated escrow ledger, released in favor of the IC only after documentary inspection, and then settled onward to the supplier by MT103.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Outright deliverable USD/WST forward contracts with tenors of up to 12 months through Samoan authorized dealers, limited to trade-backed conversion needs.

Non-deliverable forward (NDF) contracts on WST/USD with offshore bank counterparties, permitted on a hedge-only basis supported by underlying commercial exposure; speculative NDF books are prohibited by the CBS.
Cross-currency swaps (EUR/USD, CNY/USD, AUD/USD) with licensed bank counterparties where an underlying trade payable or receivable exists; post-trade CBS notification is required.

FX swap rollovers and spot-next executions for working-capital alignment between payable and receivable value dates using the same authorized-dealer relationship; options and exotic derivatives are not routinely permitted and require prior CBS approval.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual International Company Licence Fee (government renewal fee; no annual return is filed for a Samoa International Company)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registrar of International Companies, Samoa Companies Office, Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour (MCIL), Samoa
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within the anniversary month of incorporation, being 30 days before or after each anniversary of registration
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late payment attracts a default penalty of 10% of the unpaid annual fee; with continued non-payment for approximately three consecutive months after the anniversary, the Registrar may publish a strike-off notice in the Samoa Gazette and administratively dissolve the company without court order

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Return and Audited Financial Statements Filing — statutory exemption (no filing obligation for International Companies)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: None — Samoa International Companies are expressly exempt from filing annual returns or financial statements with the Registrar under the International Companies Act 1987 (as amended)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Not applicable; the sole recurring statutory obligation is payment of the annual licence fee, after which the company may obtain a Certificate of Good Standing

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No compulsory audit threshold applies to a standard Samoa International Company engaged in wholesale trading. A mandatory independent audit is triggered only for regulated licensees (e.g., international banks, international insurance companies), companies listed on a securities exchange, or companies failing audit-related solvency criteria imposed by their registered agent or a foreign parent bank covenant.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: International Financial Reporting Standards (IFRS) as issued by the IASB or a substantially equivalent accounting framework (e.g., UK GAAP or US GAAP) may be adopted voluntarily. The International Companies Act requires only the maintenance of accounting records sufficient to show and explain transactions and to disclose, with reasonable accuracy, the financial position of the company at any time. No financial statements need be filed with the Registrar.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Samoa imposes no separate annual beneficial-ownership return. The registered agent must collect and verify beneficial ownership information at client onboarding and must refresh and confirm such information at least annually, in practice at the annual licence-fee anniversary. Any transfer of shares or change of control must be reported to the registered agent within 14 days so that the beneficial-ownership register is updated, and the agent must produce the register to the Registrar or the Financial Intelligence Unit upon lawful request.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Charges (if any encumbrance has been registered)
Beneficial Ownership Register (maintained by the registered agent at the registered office)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 400 - 1,200 per year, depending on the service provider and the level of corporate secretarial support included
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 2,000 - 5,000 per engagement, applicable only when an audit is voluntarily commissioned by shareholders, a foreign parent, or a financing bank; no statutory audit is mandated for this entity

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 0% for qualifying International Companies (IC) under the International Companies Act 2015; the general Samoan corporate income tax rate for taxable resident companies is 27%.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Full statutory exemption on foreign-source income, capital gains, and offshore trading profit. No stamp duty, no capital duty, no VAT/GST applicable to ICs. The only recurring charge is the annual government license fee (WST 500–5,000 depending on issued share capital). Income from Samoan domestic operations would break the exemption and subject the IC to the 27% corporate rate.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: CIT-1 (Samoa Company Income Tax Return) – Ministry of Revenue and Taxation e-Services portal. Not applicable to a qualifying International Company unless the exemption has been lost by carrying on business in Samoa.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: For taxable Samoan companies: due 6 months after the end of the income year (standard financial year ends 30 June). Non-resident ICs are exempt from CIT-1 filing, provided no Samoa-sourced business activity is conducted.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter 0 if the IC exemption is valid. Any fees, interest, rents, royalties, or sales physically supplied in Samoa must be reported.
Do not claim deductions on exempt foreign income. Keep records showing the absence of Samoan-source trading activities.
Not required for CIT-exempt ICs, but must be prepared on request to demonstrate arm's-length pricing and to support economic substance filings.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing: initial penalty WST 200 plus daily surcharge of WST 50 up to 90 days. False return: fine up to WST 50,000 or imprisonment up to 3 years. For ICs that lose their exemption, underpayment triggers the 27% corporate tax plus 200% tax penalty and daily interest at 2% per month.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: IC-AR (International Company Annual Return) – electronic lodgment via the Samoa Companies Online Registry (Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within 45 days after the anniversary of incorporation (Registrar practice). An annual government license fee is payable at the same time.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Company name and IC registration number
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Insert the exact name as shown on the Certificate of Incorporation and the unique IC number.
Must be the physical office address of the licensed registered agent; no PO Box alone is acceptable.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Directors, shareholders, and ultimate beneficial owners (UBOs)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: List all non-resident directors and shareholders, including nominee relationships and UBOs of any corporate shareholder.
Confirm that the IC has not carried on business within Samoa during the reporting year and remains entitled to the exemption.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late annual return: fixed penalty WST 500 plus WST 100 per month of delay. Failure to pay the annual license fee may result in automatic strike-off, restoration costs, and personal liability for the registered agent fees.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 0% for dividends paid by a qualifying International Company to non-resident shareholders. For ordinary resident Samoan companies, the statutory non-resident dividend withholding tax rate is 20%, unless reduced by a double taxation agreement.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: No treaty relief is required for IC distributions because they are exempt from Samoan withholding tax. For ordinary Samoan companies, the non-resident shareholder must submit to the Ministry of Revenue: (i) Samoa tax ID of the payer; (ii) a Certificate of Residence (TRC) issued by the treaty jurisdiction; (iii) Form WHT-3 'Dividend Treaty Relief Claim'; and (iv) a beneficial ownership declaration. Approval typically reduces the dividend WHT to a 10–15% treaty rate for the relevant income year.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: 0% for royalty and interest payments made by a Samoa IC, because the IC is tax-exempt and payments are not derived from Samoan sources. For taxable Samoan sources, the statutory rates are 20% on royalties and 20% on interest; treaty rates generally range from 10% to 15% depending on the beneficiary's residence and the applicable double taxation agreement.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: No statutory WST threshold is codified for transfer pricing documentation; Samoa applies the arm's-length principle to all controlled transactions. In administrative practice, the Revenue Department will request contemporaneous Local File / Master File documentation where aggregate controlled turnover exceeds WST 2,000,000 in a fiscal year.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Applicable. Samoa's International Companies (Economic Substance) Regulations apply to ICs engaged in relevant activities, including wholesale distribution and service centre operations. A semiconductor/CPU/SSD wholesale trading IC must report (i) core income-generating activities performed in Samoa; (ii) adequate physical premises in Samoa; (iii) full-time local employees proportionate to the activity; and (iv) local operating expenditure sufficient to support the trade. A distribution and service centre classification will not be satisfied by passive invoicing alone.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax Evasion – Abuse of the International Company Exemption
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using the IC to carry on wholesale trading physically in Samoa – e.g., maintaining a Samoan warehouse, invoicing Samoan distribution customers, or arranging profitable sales with Samoan suppliers – while declaring nil income and maintaining the tax-exempt status.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Automatic loss of the IC exemption; assessment of corporate income tax at 27% on all undeclared Samoan-source profits; civil penalty of 100% to 200% of the tax understated; daily interest of 2% per month; criminal fine up to WST 50,000 and imprisonment up to 3 years for intentional under-reporting.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors are jointly and severally liable for the unpaid corporate tax. The Supreme Court may issue travel bans, confiscation orders, and director disqualification for up to 10 years; the corporate veil is pierced where the IC acted as the direct instrument of the directors' fraud.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Maintaining a registered office and annual return in Samoa but having no physical office, no local employees, no board meetings in Samoa, and no decision-making functions, while booking multi-million-dollar CPU/SSD brokerage turnover.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Penalties under the Economic Substance Regulations: fine up to WST 100,000 for a false substance declaration, plus continuing penalties of WST 10,000 per month; possible default assessment of tax on deemed Samoan-source income; the company may be struck off or de-registered.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be named in a tax claim, subject to civil restitution of all avoided taxes, banned from leaving Samoa until the fine is settled, and disqualified as officers of any Samoan company for up to 10 years.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Routing proceeds of spot semiconductor trading through layered Samoa IC bank accounts, using inflated or deflated invoices for SSD/CPU shipments, accepting third-party wire payments without due diligence, or structuring transactions to evade the AML reporting threshold of WST 20,000.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Money laundering offence under Samoa's Crimes Act 2013 and Anti-Money Laundering and Counter-Terrorism Financing Act: fine up to WST 1,000,000 and/or imprisonment up to 14 years; asset freezing and forfeiture; multiple offences carry cumulative penalties.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors face separate criminal prosecution, personal confiscation of assets, travel bans, designation as high-risk persons, and prohibition from holding financial or corporate office. A director who knowingly signs false wires or invoice records is criminally liable as a principal.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Filing an Annual Return that conceals the ultimate beneficial owner, using an unlicensed nominee director without disclosing control, or submitting false UBO information to the Registrar of International Companies.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Fine up to WST 20,000 per false entry; company strike-off; referral to the Samoa Financial Intelligence Unit; prosecution for false declaration carries imprisonment up to 5 years and confiscation of benefits derived from the concealed ownership.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors are personally liable for all penalties; the court may issue a travel ban pending full disclosure; the nominee director is jointly liable and may be prohibited from acting as an officer in Samoa or abroad under mutual legal assistance measures.
